 ## Introduction: A Humble Experiment 

 I went into mva hackathon with little to no background in genetics. To me, a genome was just a massive text file. I wanted to build an experimental
 tool to bridge the gap between finding a 1D genomic mutation in a VCF file and visualizing its 3D structural impact, without needing a PhD to operate
 it. 

 I built OmniStrand—a React and TypeScript web app that parses patient VCF files 100% locally in the browser for absolute privacy. To make it
 accessible, I integrated a custom WebMCP (Model Context Protocol) architecture. This allows an autonomous LLM agent to literally pilot the user
 interface—automatically typing in coordinates, navigating the genome browser, and pulling up the 3D AlphaFold structures via PDBe-Molstar. 

 ## The Submission: A Perfect Score 

 I used this experimental tool as my actual pipeline for the hackathon's clinical benchmark. I loaded the patient VCF into OmniStrand, and the WebMCP
 agent took over the UI. It successfully navigated the genome, identified the compound heterozygous mutation responsible for Mosaic Variegated
 Aneuploidy (MVA), resolved the UniProt ID, and highlighted the mutated residue on the 3D protein model. 

 The AI then generated my clinical CSV payload directly from the UI. Despite my lack of prior genetics experience, I submitted that exact payload for
 Track 1, and it was accepted with a perfect score. 

 ## Future Improvements 

 While OmniStrand successfully automated a clinical workflow, this is just the foundation. My next steps for the project include: 

 • Multi-Agent Orchestration: Expanding the WebMCP toolset so multiple AI agents can collaborate in the UI (e.g., one agent parses the genome while
 another simultaneously queries pharmacological databases for drug interactions).
 • In-Browser Molecular Docking: Upgrading the 3D Discovery Engine to support basic ligand-docking simulations, allowing researchers to test drug
 repurposing directly in the browser.
 • Wasm-Powered Genomics: Replacing the JavaScript VCF parser with a WebAssembly (Wasm) implementation to handle massive whole-genome sequencing (WGS)
 files with zero lag.
